newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen to take 60 pct of steel venture.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen to take 60 pct of steel venture.

text.p: Thyssen AG will take a 60 percent share in its proposed steel joint venture with Krupp-Hoesch, Hans-Wilhelm Grasshoff, chief of Krupp's steel operation, told a workforce meeting late on Tuesday.
The joint venture company is due to be founded on April 1, but production in the two companies steel units is likely to continue as before until mid- to late-1998, he said.
Thereafter, production is likely to be switched between plants owned by the two groups in the Ruhr valley towns of Dortmund and Duisberg with a so far unspecified impact on jobs.
Thyssen was expected to take the majority share of the new steel venture because it has the largest existing capacity and its operations are seen as more profitable than those of Krupp.
